title: Claudinite task declaration
description: A tasks/<name>/task.json: what a task is, when it runs — its preconditions, cadence included — and what its run does to pull requests. The runtime contract is packs/claudinite-tasks/task-contract.mjs; the enums here mirror its lists and a test holds them in step. Absent, automerge is nothing and agent_model is none; preconditions and the timeouts have no default.

id.description: The task's name — the same as its directory name.

description.description: What the task does, or why it exists, in at most fifty words — never what the other fields already say (the cadence, the conditions, the policy, the files).

frequency.description: The retired cadence field; read at the door as the first condition it always meant (`due:<cadence>`) with a `schedule` trigger, and `manual` as no condition at all with a `request` trigger. Write those two fields instead.

trigger.description: Who mints an occurrence of this task. `schedule` is asked by the scheduler at every tick, and runs when its `preconditions` hold. `request` is asked by nobody: it runs only from an item somebody creates — a marked issue, a wake, a chain link, a fan-out target — at whose pick those same conditions are judged. A declaration stating no trigger is read off the shape of its `preconditions` for one convergence window (#1789).

preconditions.description: When the task runs — every listed condition must hold, `||` between alternatives. A cadence first where the task keeps one (`due:daily|weekly|monthly` on the repo's schedule, or `last-run-over:<12h|1d|7d>`), `last-run-not-failed` to stop past the task's own failure park, then the built-in movement terms (e.g. "substantive-change", "commits-under:<dir>") or terms the task's own preconditions.mjs exports. The same conditions are judged whether the run was asked for by the scheduler or by a person, so this field never says WHETHER the task is on the schedule — `trigger` does. A scheduled task with no cadence term is asked at every tick and runs whenever its other conditions hold; a task with no conditions at all runs whenever an occurrence exists.

expected_outcome.description: What the run does to pull requests, resolved once by the executor and handed to both phases: `no_code_changes` opens none; `fresh_pr` opens one on a freshly minted branch and leaves the task's earlier pull requests alone; `amend_existing_or_create_new_pr` pushes onto the task's newest open pull request while it has no conflicts, a fresh branch otherwise; `supersede_existing_pr` takes a fresh branch and closes the task's earlier pull requests once its own exists (a green, unlanded one on an auto-merge repo is landed instead). The retired `none`/`pr` normalize to the first two.

automerge.description: What may land unreviewed, beside any expected_outcome that opens a pull request: "nothing", "anything", or a list of diff classes, each optionally reject:-prefixed and narrowable with `&&`. Optional: defaults to "nothing".

agent_model.description: The model family the agentic phase runs at; `none` runs no agent. Optional: defaults to `none`.

agent_instructions.description: The worker spec the agent session reads, a file beside this declaration (conventionally task.md). Required beside an agent_model other than none; no default.

agent_execution_timeout.description: Seconds bounding the agentic run — generous; extreme protection, not a scheduling knob. Required beside an agent_model other than none: a running agent always has a bound.

code_work.description: The deterministic first phase: a command run with the task directory as cwd, e.g. "node worker.mjs". Task-local — no absolute path, no `..`. Optional: absent, there is no code work.

code_work_timeout.description: Seconds after which the code_work subprocess is killed and the task fails. Required beside code_work: a subprocess always has a bound.

schedule_after.description: Task ids ("<pack>/<task>") this task yields to while their items are live this cycle.

on_interrupt.description: What happens to the work item when a recovery path would re-execute it. Default `requeue`; `needs-human` for a genuinely one-shot side effect.

invocation_endpoint.description: A key in the repo's taskScheduler.agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints — never a URL — for a task needing reach an ordinary session in its repo does not have.

code_work_required_secrets.description: The repo Actions secret names the code-work phase needs configured — the phase that runs Action-side, where a secret exists. Never GITHUB_* or CLAUDINITE_*.

required_secrets.description: The retired spelling of code_work_required_secrets; normalized at the door. Rename it.

model_from_request.description: Reserved to the engine's built-in request task: run at the model the work item names.

session_scope.description: Read by nothing since #974. Drop it; name an invocation_endpoint if the task needs wider reach.
